entry.summary:
Welcome to Auckland University of Technology’s (AUT) Research Matters! 🚀 AUT’s Research Matters video series is where AUT academics answer everyday questions about their fields of expertise. Get the answer to those questions you’ve always had – or maybe never knew to ask.   

Do mass murderers have the same human rights as everyone else?  Do some people have more human rights than others? Lida Ayoubi, Senior Lecturer at AUT Law School, is here to answer your questions about human rights.  

00:00 Introduction 
00:27 Is everyone equal when it comes to human rights and does everyone have them?  
01:38 What exactly are “human rights”?  
02:51 What is the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights – and why was it written?  
03:58 So if the UN Declaration of Human Rights was written in 1948, does it ever get updated?  
05:05 How does New Zealand uphold the human rights of Kiwis?  
06:04 Do some people have more human rights than others?  
07:00 Are we living in a time when, internationally, human rights are at their most vulnerable?  
08:21 How does NZ stack up internationally when it comes to human rights?  
08:55 Is everyone entitled to have their human rights protected? What about mass murderers and pedophiles?  
09:41 Has the world made progress when it comes to ensuring human rights for all?  
10:34 Could there be new human rights in the future?  

📖 Read about Lida Ayoubi  https://academics.aut.ac.nz/lida.ayoubi  
🎓Interested in studying at AUT Law School? https://www.aut.ac.nz/study/study-options/law   
⚖️ Read about the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights: https://www.un.org/en/about-us/universal-declaration-of-human-rights   
Te Kāhui Tika Tangata Human Rights Commission: https://tikatangata.org.nz/   
Ombudsman Tuia Kia Oritē: https://www.ombudsman.parliament.nz/   
Privacy Commissioner Te Mana Mātāpono Matatapu:  https://www.privacy.org.nz/
